([[Irondequoit, New York]]) | college = [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]] (2017–2020) | draft_year = 2021 | years1 = 2023–2025 | team1 = [[Reales de La Vega]] | years2 = 2025–present | team2 = [[Gaiteros del Zulia]] }} '''Nahziah Carter''' (born August 24, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Gaiteros del Zulia]] of the [[Superliga Profesional de Baloncesto]] (SPB). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]]. ==Early life== Carter grew up in [[Rochester, New York]], and attended [[Bishop Kearney High School (Irondequoit, New York)|Bishop Kearney High School]]. He averaged 15.1 points per game as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/washington/Article/Washington-officially-adds-Nahziah-Carter-to-the-class-of-2017-53338719/|title=Washington officially adds Nahziah Carter to the class of 2017|first=Kyle|last=Latos|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=June 26, 2017|access-date=January 26, 2020}} As a senior, Carter averaged 19.1 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/college/university-of-washington/huskies-insider-blog/article158324694.html|title=Nahziah Carter is officially a member of the Huskies men’s basketball program|first=Christian|last=Caple|work=[[The News Tribune]]|date=June 26, 2017|access-date=January 26, 2020}} Rated a four-star recruit, Carter originally committed to play college basketball at [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] but re-opened his recruitment after [[Archie Miller (basketball)|Archie Miller]] left to become the head coach at [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]]. Carter eventually committed to play at Washington over offers from [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] and [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]].{{cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/nahziah-carter-jay-z-nephew-washington-basketball-recruiting|title=Nahziah Carter, Jay-Z's nephew, commits to Washington basketball|website=USATodayHSS.com|access-date=January 26, 2020}} ==College career== As a true freshman, Carter averaged 5.1 points and 1.7 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.bellinghamherald.com/sports/college/pac-12/university-of-washington/article221840675.html|title=Sophomore Nahziah Carter doesn’t lack confidence. He’s been key for Huskies off the bench|first=Lauren|last=Kirschman|work=[[The Bellingham Herald]]|date=November 18, 2018|access-date=January 26, 2020}} He averaged 8.1 points and 2.4 rebounds per game and scored at least ten points in 15 games as a key reserve in his sophomore season.{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/uws-nahziah-carter-is-a-great-angler-and-a-better-hooper-heres-why-hes-about-to-reel-in-big-numbers/|title=UW’s Nahziah Carter is a great angler and a better hooper. Here’s why he’s about to reel in big numbers.|first=Percy|last=Allen|work=[[The Seattle Times]]|date=November 1, 2019|access-date=January 26, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/college/university-of-washington/article228354879.html|title=Nahziah Carter, Jamal Bey show UW's future|work=[[The News Tribune]]|date=March 24, 2019|access-date=January 26, 2020}} Carter entered his junior season as the Huskies' leading returning scorer.{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/nahziah-carter-scores-17-and-isaiah-stewart-16-to-lead-uw-huskies-in-blowout-exhibition-win/|title=Nahziah Carter scores 18 and Isaiah Stewart 16 to lead UW Huskies in blowout exhibition win|first=Percy|last=Allen|work=[[The Seattle Times]]|date=August 15, 2019|access-date=January 26, 2020}} He scored a career-high 23 points with seven rebounds in the Huskies season opening win over 16th-ranked [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rochesterfirst.com/sports/college-sports/roc-natives-isaiah-stewart-nahziah-carter-shine-in-upset-over-no-16-baylor/|title=ROC natives Isaiah Stewart, Nahziah Carter shine in upset over No. 16 Baylor|website=[[WROC-TV|RochesterFirst.com]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 10, 2019|access-date=January 26, 2020}} Carter scored 18 points and grabbed 12 rebounds against [[Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball|Tennessee]] for his first career double-double in a 75–62 loss.{{cite web|url=https://thehuskyhaul.com/2019/11/17/washington-basketball-falls-tennessee/|title=Washington basketball falls to Tennessee|first=Herbert|last=Nightingale|website=TheHuskyHaul.com|publisher=[[FanSided]]|date=November 17, 2019|access-date=January 26, 2020}} He was the Huskies's third-leading scorer and rebounder as a junior with 12.2 points and 4.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Nightingale |first1=Herbert |title=A look back at Washington basketball’s 2019-20 season |url=https://thehuskyhaul.com/2020/03/31/look-back-washington-basketball-2019-20-season/ |website=The Husky Haul |publisher=FanSided |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |date=March 31, 2020}} Carter was suspended from team activities on October 15, 2020, due to two separate sexual assault allegations that were found to be true.{{cite news |last1=Shah |first1=Ash |last2=Yamashita |first2=Andy |last3=Goldstein |first3=Jake |title=University investigation found basketball player Nahziah Carter sexually assaulted two students |url=http://www.dailyuw.com/news/article_5e752186-374c-11eb-874a-87a1e760ea27.html |access-date=December 7, 2020 |work=[[The Daily of the University of Washington|The Daily]] |date=December 5, 2020}}
